one_liner: TensorFlow.js backend that runs XNNPACK C++ kernels compiled to WebAssembly; 3-20x faster than the plain-JS CPU backend for CNN inference.
what_it_does: @tensorflow/tfjs-backend-wasm is a registered TensorFlow.js backend. You import it and call `await tf.setBackend('wasm')`, and existing tf.GraphModel or LayersModel code runs unchanged: MobileNet, BlazeFace, BodyPix, PoseDetection, USE and the other listed tfjs-models. At startup it feature-detects WebAssembly SIMD and threads and loads one of three binaries: tfjs-backend-wasm.wasm, -simd.wasm or -threaded-simd.wasm. setWasmPaths points it at self-hosted binaries, and setThreadsCount sets the size of the XNNPACK thread pool.
how_it_is_fast: Hot ops such as convolutions, depthwise convolutions, matmul, pooling and PReLU run XNNPACK's hand-tuned f32 micro-kernels. They are compiled with Emscripten (emsdk 3.1.28, bazel -c opt, C++17, -fno-rtti, -fno-exceptions, emmalloc), with -msimd128 for the SIMD builds and -pthread plus an 8-worker pthreadpool for the threaded build. Data lives in the wasm heap, and kernels are called through cwrap. The baseline it beats is TensorFlow.js's own tfjs-backend-cpu, which runs scalar JavaScript loops over typed arrays.
when_to_use: CPU inference of small CNNs (about 20-60M multiply-adds, e.g. BlazeFace or face detectors), where the README tables show WASM matching or beating WebGL (MacBook Pro 15 2019 Face Detector: 13.6 ms WASM, 7.9 ms WASM+SIMD, 4.0 ms with threads, vs 22.7 ms WebGL).
Devices or browsers where WebGL is missing, blocklisted or numerically unreliable. The FAQ says WASM has better numerical stability and wider device support.
Any TF.js app still on the plain-JS CPU backend. MobileNet V2 runs 3.0-12.1x faster on the base WASM build alone (derived from page data), and much more with SIMD and threads.
Pages that can send COOP/COEP headers, which unlocks the threaded-SIMD binary (ThinkPad X1 Gen6 MobileNet V2: 12.4 ms vs 34.6 ms SIMD-only).
when_not_to_use: Medium or large models (100-500M multiply-adds) on a working GPU. WebGL is 2.4-7.7x faster than plain WASM for MobileNet V2 on every device in the README. Only the threaded-SIMD build beat WebGL, on the two desktop rows that have it (ThinkPad 12.4 vs 44.8 ms; MacBook 10.3 vs 19.6 ms, a cross-run pair).

Node.js servers. Multithreading is disabled under Node (flags_wasm.ts, issue #3830), and the README's Node 14 row is 64.2 ms with SIMD vs 10.3 ms threaded in Chrome on the same MacBook. Use tfjs-node (native TensorFlow) or a native runtime instead.
Training. The FAQ says gradient ops are incomplete and the focus is inference, and unsupported ops throw 'not yet implemented'.

New long-lived projects that need an actively updated runtime. The backend's last functional change was in September 2023, a May 2023 XNNPACK upgrade was reverted for lack of maintainer bandwidth, and the build still pins XNNPACK commit 5e8033a7.

Cross-origin-isolated threading is not possible on your host. Without COOP/COEP the backend falls back to SIMD-only, which is 2.8-2.9x slower for MobileNet V2 on the README's desktop rows (1.3-2.0x for Face Detector).

integration.dependencies: @tensorflow/tfjs-core (peer) and @tensorflow/tfjs-backend-cpu; bundles XNNPACK, pthreadpool, cpuinfo, FP16 and FXdiv inside the .wasm files
integration.min_toolchain: Runtime: any browser or Node with WebAssembly (SIMD and threads optional, auto-detected); building from source needs Bazel with the emsdk 3.1.28 toolchain, which the build fetches itself
integration.platforms: browsers (desktop and mobile), Node.js (single-threaded), WeChat miniprogram build; threads need SharedArrayBuffer plus COOP/COEP since Chrome 92
integration.thread_safety: single JS-thread API; intra-op parallelism through XNNPACK's pthreadpool in Web Workers (pool of 8 pre-created workers, default threads = logical cores / 2 capped at 8)

gotchas: Benchmark tables are assembled from several runs. The WASM, WebGL and Plain JS columns date from December 2019 (commit 60a91b8 onward). The WASM+SIMD column was added in June 2020 (5db28e7, 4114cad), threads in August 2020 (f580dfc), and the Pixel 4, ThinkPad and Node rows on 2020-08-26 (b35e9f5), each with newer XNNPACK and Emscripten builds. The header still says all runs were Chrome 79, but SIMD then needed chrome://flags or an origin trial (issue #3896). So SIMD-or-threads vs Plain JS ratios on the MacBook, Windows and Face Detector Desktop Linux rows compare different runs. The prose ranges (3X-11.5X faster than JS, 5.3-7.7X slower than WebGL) were computed from the 2019 rows: 11.5X is a Desktop Linux 91.5 vs 1049 ms row that has since been replaced.
The README says the default thread count is the number of logical cores, but backend.cc uses emscripten_num_logical_cores()/2, capped at 8 (the pre-created PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE).

Self-hosting needs all three .wasm files (and the worker script for threads) served with correct paths and CORS/CORP headers. Bundlers must leave the .wasm assets alone, and terser's 'typeofs' compress option breaks the threaded build with '_scriptDir is not defined'.

If the SIMD binary fails to load (wrong setWasmPaths, missing file), the backend silently runs the much slower non-SIMD build. Issue #7739 (2023, closed by a stale bot in 2026) is a user seeing about 10x slower than WebGL and unable to tell which binary or XNNPACK path was active.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other neural-network inference runtime is catalogued in this category. Pick it over hand-written wasm numeric libraries such as Ubique (nalgebra) or kmeans-wasm when you already have a TensorFlow.js graph or layers model and want its CPU path sped up without code changes. The siblings are narrower kernels you would call yourself.
verified_claims_summary: The first-party README tables report average inference time over 200 runs on the TF.js benchmark page. On a ThinkPad X1 Gen6 (Linux), MobileNet V2 takes 122.7 ms with plain WASM, 34.6 ms with SIMD and 12.4 ms with SIMD plus threads, vs 1489.4 ms on the plain-JS CPU backend and 44.8 ms on WebGL. On iPhone XS it is 140 vs 426.4 ms (3.0x). Face Detector on desktop Linux is 12.6 vs 249.5 ms (19.8x). Runs date from December 2019 to August 2020, CPU models are not stated, and the per-column builds and browsers differ.
status_note: Stale but not archived: the backend directory's last functional commit was in September 2023 and the last edit (a README typo fix) on 2024-04-12, in a 19.1k-star Apache-2.0 monorepo whose issues are mostly closed by a stale bot. It is still usable and drop-in for existing TF.js apps, but the benchmarks are six years old and the XNNPACK pin was never refreshed.
